description: Task type base. Abstract: concrete task types are derived at runtime by consuming gears (not shipped here) and determine the input/output payload contracts. The engine stores base task fields (state, priority, queue, owner, assignment, timestamps) in indexed relational columns and the GTS-typed extension data (input, context, output) as compressed binary blobs (ADR-0006) — new task types never require DDL changes (PRD cpt-cf-task-engine-fr-gts-task-type). A derived type MAY declare concurrency limits, a derived dedup identity with optional supersession, progress settings, and type defaults (default_queue, timeouts, retry_policy, retention_days) via traits (x-gts-traits-schema). Type defaults resolve as: task creation request, then this trait, then the queue's effective value (PRD cpt-cf-task-engine-fr-gts-task-type, Type defaults resolution). Trait keys use snake_case per platform GTS convention; the engine validates the dedup/supersede traits against the type's input schema when it first resolves the type (DESIGN cpt-cf-task-engine-design-gts-types).

input.description: Validated task input payload. Derived task types narrow this with their own JSON Schema; the engine validates a task's input against the resolved schema at creation when one is registered (PRD cpt-cf-task-engine-fr-structured-io).

context.description: Optional mutable execution context (checkpoint data merged at the key level). Counted toward the aggregate payload size limit together with input and output.

output.description: Optional structured result payload set at completion. Derived task types narrow this with their own JSON Schema; validated at the completion boundary when a schema is registered

global_concurrency_limit.description: Maximum number of simultaneously executing (claimed + running) tasks of this type across all tenants. 0 or absent means unlimited. Overridable in config by GTS task-type pattern (PRD cpt-cf-task-engine-fr-type-concurrency, cpt-cf-task-engine-fr-concurrency-overrides).

per_tenant_concurrency_limit.description: Maximum number of simultaneously executing (claimed + running) tasks of this type per tenant. 0 or absent means unlimited.

dedup.description: Derived dedup identity: makes the engine compute a task's identity from the work itself rather than from a caller-supplied Idempotency-Key (PRD cpt-cf-task-engine-fr-derived-dedup). Validated against the type's input schema on first resolution; an invalid policy makes the type non-creatable (fail closed).

key_fields.description: Ordered list of RFC 6901 JSON Pointers into the task input whose values form the identity. Each pointer MUST resolve to a field the input schema declares required; at most 16 pointers; each resolved value at most 4 KiB.

scope.description: Whose tasks may collide: 'subject' (default; the creating subject), 'authz_scope' (callers whose PDP-compiled access scope is identical; NOT AVAILABLE YET — the engine rejects a type that declares it until ToolKit confirms a stable serialized form of AccessScope, PRD §11 Assumptions), or 'tenant' (all callers of the owning tenant — must be declared explicitly, never a default). owner_tenant_id is always part of the identity, so identities never cross tenants.

window.description: How long the identity stays occupied: 'active' (default; released on any terminal outcome) or 'active_or_succeeded' (additionally held after a completed task with result success/warning until retention).

supersede.description: Optional supersession policy; only valid on a type that also declares dedup (PRD cpt-cf-task-engine-fr-task-supersede). Newer order wins, equal is a replay, older is stale. A supersede-enabled type MUST NOT accept tasks with cancellable=false.

order_field.description: RFC 6901 JSON Pointer to a required, non-negative integer in the input (e.g. a graph revision). Excluded from key_fields; the engine appends its value to the dedup identity and uses the identity without it as the supersede group.

mode.description: How an obsolete in-flight task is stopped: 'graceful' (default; cancel_requested + grace period) or 'forced' (lease invalidated immediately).

authority.description: Creator authority (PRD cpt-cf-task-engine-fr-worker-principals, Creator authority; DESIGN cpt-cf-task-engine-design-creator-authority). Workers act as themselves, so this trait states whose rights bound what they do for a task. 'creator_verified' (default): at creation the engine asks the PDP, with the creator's own security context and the task's owner tenant, whether each check's action is allowed on each referenced resource; a denial, an unreachable PDP, or a result the engine cannot fully evaluate rejects the create. Checked resource references are stored and published as verified. 'worker': the work uses only the worker's authority; allowed only for platform-owned types (a tenant-owned type declaring it cannot be created). Absent means 'creator_verified' with no checks: nothing is verified and every resource reference is stored with verified = false.

checks.description: Creator checks, only with mode 'creator_verified'. At most trust_limits.max_creator_checks (default 16) entries.

source.description: Where the checked resources are named: 'resource_refs' (every resource reference whose type matches resource_type), or an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer to a field the input schema declares required and of type string, whose value is a resource ID of resource_type.

resource_type.description: GTS type identifier, or a GTS pattern with a trailing '*' when source is 'resource_refs', of the referenced resources. With a pointer source it MUST be a concrete type.

action.description: Action the work performs on the resource, as known to the PDP for that resource type (for example 'read', 'update').

progress_events.description: Progress event mode for tasks of this type (PRD cpt-cf-task-engine-fr-progress-events): 'none' (default), 'milestones' (event only when milestone/current_stage changed), or 'all' (event when any progress dimension changed). Overridable in config by task-type pattern; config override > queue override > this trait > queue registration > global default.

progress_flush_interval_secs.description: Flush interval (seconds) for batched progress persistence and derived progress events. Effective value is clamped to progress_min_flush_interval_secs.

default_queue.description: Queue for tasks of this type when the creation request names none. Absent means the 'default' queue. MUST reference a queue of kind 'dispatch' that accepts the type (accepted_types) and, if a task-domain type rule matches the type, is routed to that domain (otherwise creates without a queue are rejected TASK_DOMAIN_MISMATCH); a tenant-owned type MUST NOT name an 'operated_by: platform' queue (checked by the engine when it resolves the type, PRD cpt-cf-task-engine-fr-type-trust).

timeouts.description: Default timeouts for tasks of this type. Each field resolves on its own: task creation request, then this trait, then the queue's effective value. Copy of the queue base type's timeouts object (GTS $ref does not allow JSON Pointer fragments); keep the two in sync.

queue_timeout_secs.description: Maximum time a task may wait in 'queued' before it is force-completed as timed out (terminal).

assignment_timeout_secs.description: Maximum time a claimed task may remain 'claimed' before it starts (assignment_deadline); on expiry it is a liveness failure and the task is requeued with backoff against max_liveness_requeues (not max_retries).

execution_timeout_secs.description: Maximum running time per attempt (execution_deadline, re-armed on each start so time spent waiting is never counted). Terminal, task-attributed, never retried. Every task has an execution timeout: null/absent here falls through to the next level (task request, then type trait, then queue) and finally to the engine default default_execution_timeout_secs; it never means 'no limit'. Values above the engine trust limit (trust_limits max_execution_timeout_secs, tighter for tenant-owned types) make the type non-creatable or the queue refuse new tasks (PRD cpt-cf-task-engine-fr-timeouts, cpt-cf-task-engine-fr-type-trust).

heartbeat_timeout_secs.description: Lease duration: the maximum interval between worker heartbeats before the lease expires; falls back to default_lease_duration_secs when null. Workers MUST heartbeat at the heartbeat_interval_secs returned on claim (one third of this value, rounded down, minimum 1) so a single delayed heartbeat does not expire the lease. An expired lease is a liveness failure: the task is requeued with backoff against max_liveness_requeues (not max_retries).

lifetime_timeout_secs.description: Absolute wall-clock budget from creation to terminal state, surviving requeues. On expiry the task is force-completed as timed out (overrides retry/lease handling).

retry_policy.description: Default retry policy for tasks of this type. Taken as a whole from the first level that declares one: task creation request, then this trait, then the queue's effective value. Copy of the queue base type's retry_policy object (GTS $ref does not allow JSON Pointer fragments); keep the two in sync.

max_retries.description: Maximum number of retries after explicit retryable failures reported by a worker. Liveness requeues (lease expiry, assignment timeout) do not consume this budget; see max_liveness_requeues.

max_liveness_requeues.description: Maximum number of liveness requeues (lease expiry or assignment timeout) before the task is routed terminally with a timed_out result. Counted separately from max_retries so losing the worker never burns the failure-retry budget. Backoff uses this policy's strategy and intervals, applied to the liveness-requeue count. 0 means unlimited (bounded only by the lifetime timeout, if any).

strategy.description: Backoff strategy used to compute run_after for a retry.

max_interval_secs.description: Maximum backoff interval in seconds (caps exponential/linear growth). MUST be greater than or equal to base_interval_secs; the engine rejects a queue whose policy breaks this rule when it resolves the queue (JSON Schema cannot compare two fields).

jitter_factor.description: Fractional jitter (0.0-1.0) to de-synchronize retries. Jitter only shortens a wait: each wait is drawn from [d * (1 - jitter_factor), d], where d is the capped backoff, so it never exceeds max_interval_secs. 1.0 gives full jitter (PRD cpt-cf-task-engine-fr-retry, Backoff).

non_retryable_codes.description: Error codes that are always terminal regardless of the worker's retryable flag.

retention_days.description: Retention for terminal tasks of this type, measured from the terminal time (PRD cpt-cf-task-engine-fr-retention). Precedence: tenant policy > matching config type pattern > this trait > global default.
